# Vendored crates — provenance and re-sync

`Cact/crypto/vendor/` holds three third-party Rust trees.  They are **not**
verbatim upstream: each is upstream *pruned* of what the kernel does not build
(workspace members, fuzz/test fixtures) and *patched* in a few recorded places.
Use [`tools/vendor_sync.py`](../../../tools/vendor_sync.py) to see the exact
state and to refresh it — it fetches the upstream ref, re-applies every recorded
edit, and diffs the result against what is committed here.

| Directory | Upstream | Ref | SPDX |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rustls-0.23.40/` | <https://github.com/rustls/rustls> | tag `v/0.23.40` | `Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT` |
| `rustls-webpki/` | <https://github.com/rustls/webpki> | tag `v/0.103.11` | `ISC` |
| `rustls-pki-types/` | crates.io `rustls-pki-types` 1.12.0 | crate tarball (USTC mirror) | `MIT OR Apache-2.0` |

## What is pruned

* `rustls`: only the repo's `.cargo/`, `.github/`, dotfiles, `Cargo.toml`,
  `LICENSE*`, `README.md` and `rustls/` are vendored — the other workspace
  members (`rustls-bench`, `rustls-test`, `bogo`, `fuzz`, `test-ca`, …) are not.
  Inside `rustls/`, `src/testdata/` and `tests/data/` are dropped (megabytes of
  `.der`/`.bin` fixtures).
* `rustls-webpki`: only `Cargo.toml`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `src` and a few
  dotfiles/`.github`; `tests/`, `benches/`, `third-party/` are not vendored.
* `rustls-pki-types`: the crates.io package, minus `tests/`.

## Local edits (re-applied by the sync tool)

| Tree | File | Edit |
|---|---|---|
| rustls | `rustls/src/lib.rs` | `mod conn;` → `pub mod conn;` (cact_crypto/cact_net reach it from outside the crate) |
| rustls | `rustls/src/conn.rs` | `pub(crate) mod unbuffered;` → `pub mod unbuffered;` |
| rustls-webpki | `src/lib.rs` | drop `#[cfg(any(feature = "std", test))] extern crate std;` — the kernel has no std |

Plus one `// SPDX-License-Identifier:` line at the top of every vendored `.rs`
file (upstream ships no per-file SPDX).

## Local overrides (kept as ours; never overwritten by the tool)

| Tree | File | Why |
|---|---|---|
| rustls | `rustls/Cargo.toml` | de-workspaced: deps flattened from `workspace = true` to pinned versions, path deps on the local `rustls-webpki` / `rustls-pki-types`, unused features (`aws_lc_rs`, `ring`, `brotli`, `zlib`, `fips`, `read_buf`) dropped |
| rustls | `rustls/build.rs` | reduced to `fn main() {}` (no `rustversion` read_buf gate) |
| rustls-webpki | `Cargo.toml` | `pki-types` dep points at the local copy instead of crates.io |
| rustls-pki-types | `.cargo-checksum.json` | generated by `cargo vendor`; not part of the tarball |

`tools/vendor_sync.py check` prints how far each override has drifted from the
current upstream file — that is the thing to read on a version bump, because
upstream gaining a feature or a dep in one of those files is not visible
anywhere else.

## How the kernel builds against it

`Cact/net/rust_net/Cargo.toml` path-depends on `rustls-0.23.40/rustls` and
`rustls-pki-types`, with a `[patch.crates-io]` override for the latter.  The
crypto provider is CactOS's own (`Cact/crypto/src/provider.rs`), selected via
the `custom-provider` feature — no `ring`/`aws-lc-rs` backend is compiled.

## Re-sync procedure

```sh
python3 tools/vendor_sync.py check              # what differs, what to merge
python3 tools/vendor_sync.py check rustls-webpki
python3 tools/vendor_sync.py update rustls      # rewrite from upstream (dirty tree refused)
```

`check` is read-only.  `update` fetches, re-applies the recorded edits, keeps the
overrides, deletes anything upstream has dropped, and leaves the result for
review in `git diff` — including any edit it could not re-apply, which it reports
loudly instead of dropping silently.  After an update, re-apply the same
pruning/override decisions to the new version and re-run `check` until it says
`in sync`.  A version bump means updating the `ref`/`version` in the manifest at
the top of `tools/vendor_sync.py` and the table above.
